review_output: {"summary":"No BLOCKER found in the tenant revision slice, but this is not approval of the whole Goal. Coverage is still `unknown` and report binding to the tenant revision is known next work. What holds up: the tenant fence uses append-only rows, not a shared counter. Inserts go in old/new vendor order and only take KEY SHARE locks on Vendor (the existing FK check already takes these). Both UPDATE short-circuits cover every CommerceOrder and PaymentTransaction column the audit reads (PaymentTransaction metadata is compared whole). Blocking TRUNCATE on the commerce tables closes the gap where TRUNCATE skips row triggers. The ledger and functions are private to anon/authenticated/service_role, and the revision function counts with row security off. The audit returns only internal IDs and outcomes, uses a strict id regex and a keyset cursor, and enforces read-only repeatable read. Remaining issues: (1) MAJOR: at realistic load, per-page O(n) counts and a re-sort of the whole window on every page will push large tenants into permanent unavailable or errors (fails closed). (2) MAJOR: the new Vendor read and insert on every payment/order write in Serializable payment transactions has not been measured against the already-failing Serializable gate. (3) Dependency questions: whether existing source/registration revisions fence the other classification inputs, and whether production workers get EXECUTE. (4) The whole-tenant fence fires on irrelevant changes, which risks a future publisher never getting a stable read. (5) Timeouts throw instead of returning a bounded result. (6) Small test and fencing gaps.","findings":[{"area":"Realistic load / bounded RR wrapper","severity":"MAJOR","confidence":0.6,"file":"src/lib/live-metric-order-audit.ts","issue":"Every page re-runs three COUNT(*) revision functions over ledgers that only grow. The tenant ledger gains a row on every CommerceOrder/PaymentTransaction insert and every relevant update. The page query also filters by vendor and window and orders by o.id, so it needs either a (vendorId,id) index scan with a filter or a re-sort of the whole window on every page. Together with the 2s statement_timeout and the 20s wall budget, this makes large or busy tenants fail every time.","impact":"Fails closed (limit_exceeded or a thrown 57014 error), so it doesn't produce false coverage. But high-volume vendors may never get an enumerated audit, which blocks the later coverage proof. Tests only use 20 orders.","evidence":"Lines 20-25 run tenant/order/registration revision counts on every call. auditMetricOrderSources calls it up to 2000 times in one RR snapshot where the values cannot change. The tenant trigger inserts a row for every INSERT and every metadata/status change. No load test with large ledgers.","recommended_fix":"Compute the context and revisions once per RR transaction and pass them to later pages (assert once at the end if you want). Add or confirm an index that serves vendorId + status + createdAt window + id keyset (e.g. (vendorId, id) INCLUDE (createdAt, status, primaryPaymentTransactionId), or a window-first keyset on (createdAt, id)). Benchmark the COUNT revision on large ledgers, or plan a compacted or checkpointed revision as a dependency change.","required_test":"Seed a disposable DB with roughly 1M tenant ledger rows and 100k orders in the window. Each time it reads Vendor (line 26) and inserts a row with an FK check. In Serializable payment transactions, that Vendor read adds a predicate (SIREAD) lock on a hot per-tenant row on top of the existing scoped trigger's reads. Nobody has measured whether this raises serialization failure or retry rates.","impact":"The synchronized Serializable payment gate already FAILs for unrelated reasons. SELECT id FROM public.\"Vendor\" WHERE id=target, inside a SECURITY DEFINER AFTER ROW trigger on both payment tables. If they go up, think about narrowing which changes fire the trigger (see the over-broad fence finding) or dropping the Vendor read where the FK already guarantees the vendor exists (for example, only fall back to the existence check on DELETE or cascade paths).","required_test":"Run a synchronized concurrent Serializable payment and order workload on one vendor, with concurrent Vendor-row updates. The tenant and scoped order ledgers don't fence these. This change relies on sourceRevision and registrationRevision to do it. It hasn't been shown that those revisions change when a submission that a tenant order references (possibly one that currently has a different liveId or form) changes, or when Live.formId changes. The context check also doesn't look at collectionEnabled or the version's revoked/superseded state.","impact":"If the dependency revisions don't cover these inputs, a future publisher could check all four revisions as unchanged and still publish classifications built on stale source data.","evidence":"Lines 35-40 and 44-48 join FormSubmission by p.metadata->>'formSubmissionId' with no live scoping in the join, plus Live/RegistrationForm/LiveMetricRegistration. The fence is safe but much broader than needed.","impact":"During active selling the vendor-wide revision will change all the time. Only do this if you're confident no other reader depends on the broader fence.","required_test":"Assert the tenant revision stays the same after an irrelevant metadata key change and after a paid→shipped status change. The tenant ledger uses ON UPDATE NO ACTION while the scoped ledger uses ON UPDATE CASCADE (which the immutable trigger then rejects).
